hints.content: The arrow points to all values greater than $-8$.
So, the inequality represents everything **greater than $-8$.**

question.content:
**Choose the inequality that represents the following graph.**



[[☃ image 1]]

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A number line from negative 1 to 9 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 8. A line running to the right starts at negative 8 and continues.

choices.clue:
The graph of $ -8>x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 9 to 1 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at negative 8. A line running to the left starts at negative 8 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/ea4ddce6be9280c9c1aa889c19681ea131775611)

The graph of $1>x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 9 to 1 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 1. A line running to the left starts at 1 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/740f313cce47822c2bbaa612439160432918a377)

The graph of $ 8>x$ actually looks like this:

![A number line from negative 1 to 9 with evenly spaced tick marks in increments of 1. An open point is plotted at 8. A line running to the left starts at 8 and continues.](web+graphie:${☣ LOCALPATH}/images/e54390a6aa5a4cb654cd26e956dcc6eb948b49f9)
